summary: Donkey anaphora with strong and weak sums, after Luo 2021, built on the donkey context of Ranta.v and the Sundholm-style quantifier of Ranta_GQ.v. The Sigma type of owner-donkey-proof triples is compared with the collection of owners formed with a weak existential. Luo's formula (10) is proved with uniqueness of proofs as a displayed premise, and the bound is shown to fail for Type-valued families. The pair, strong and weak readings of 'most farmers who own a donkey beat it' are proved equal to counting forms; for 'every' they agree, and the strong reading entails the weak. On Luo's ten-farmer model the pair reading holds and both of his readings fail. Sundholm's own alternative, counting by first components with A-injections (his formula (27)), is stated as printed, and the map from his pairs to Luo's collection is proved to be of that kind. The existential encodings (9) and (22) and a restricted truncation interface cover Luo's section 4.

sources.citation: Luo, Z. (2021). On Type-Theoretical Semantics of Donkey Anaphora. The 14-page version on the author's page; its file name indicates LACL 2021. A shorter version, 'Donkey Anaphora: Type-Theoretic Semantics with Both Strong and Weak Sums', is in the proceedings of the ESSLLI 2021 workshop CSTFRS, pp. 45-52.

evidence: DRAFT for the author's review; not an accepted source-level verdict.
L21 (5), (7), (9), (12), (13), (16), (18), (22) and Appendix D are stated in the paper's own shape.
L21 (10) is proved with uniqueness of proofs as a displayed premise (card_subset_le).
L21 section 2's ten-farmer model is computed: 29 triples, 10 owners, the pair reading holds and both of Luo's readings fail, on types as well as by counting (luo_ten_farmers_type_level).
S89 (27) is stated as printed; the map from S89's pairs to L21's collection is proved to be an A-injection that identifies pairs with the same owner and is onto (forward_realizes_owner_count).
simplifications: finite types as complete duplicate-free lists
the collection of owners over an arbitrary proposition Q equivalent to owning a donkey
truncation restricted to one family of types
models are boolean tables read as propositions
omissions: UTT and Martin-Lof type theory with h-logic as type theories; the inconsistency of large Sigma-propositions and the remark on small ones (L21 section 4)
E-type anaphora (L21 section 3.3) and other quantifiers
S89's objection that his alternative loses definitional uniformity (p. 10)
the alternative definition of Most in note 4 of S89
whether the bound of L21 (10) can fail for a proposition
additions: the converse condition respects_first and the results on A-injections
bool_model_readings and the corollaries on three models

determination_rationale: DRAFT for the author. Proposed value: slight_modification. The paper's formulas transpose directly. The modifications are an explicit premise for uniqueness of proofs, lists for finite types, and the generalization of the collection of owners to a proposition Q.

artifact_classes.description: finite types as complete duplicate-free lists; card_iff_fin relates this to the bijection with Fin(n)
the collection of owners over any proposition Q equivalent to owning a donkey, not only the literal existential
models are boolean tables read as propositions; their readings on types are decided by counting
respects_first and the results built on it are a reading of S89 (27), which the paper leaves undefined
zero axioms; each principle a result depends on is an explicit premise; two results are stated in Type
